content.body:
This was the famous P-40 that introduced the air combat world to "six fifties" in early American and British Commonwealth aviation and was known in France as the H87.
France had already ordered the original H-81 variant of the P-40 when the war broke out, and the H87 was built by Curtiss to be an improved version of their most successful fighter. While still not the best in speed or climb above low/med altitudes, it did perform better than the earlier variants due to a two-stage supercharged Packard-built Merlin engine. Its rugged construction, good maneuverability, and incredible dive performance continued to serve it better than its performance on a stats sheet might suggest. Of course, part of this was the crushing lethality of six fifty-caliber heavy machine guns on the structural integrity of enemy aircraft.
This model carries the famous "Sioux Head" markings of the Lafeyette Escadrille, which was made famous in WWI when American pilots flew for France as members of that Armee de l'Air squadron.
With six of the famed Browning "Ma Duece" .50 cal heavy machine guns in the wings the H87 can do well in low altitude fights where its performance better matches that of the high altitude capable Axis fighters, like the Bf 109. While the H87 does outperform the H81 at higher altitudes, the enemy fighters still gain a significant margin up high.
You can turn and burn with the 109s down low, as long as you understand you need to turn initially hard and get a guns solution to lay on all that .50 caliber love, because in a sustained flat turn the 109s will out turn you and they can out climb you too. Go in with some dive speed and clobber them quick, yanking hard if needed for a burst of HMG destruction and then unload the airframe (back off the stick) and extend for another pass after maybe a zoom climb. Fly with at least one or two buddies because this isn't an all around superior performing fighter, even if it does have a wicked set of guns that can kill quickly.
content.brief: TYPE: Fighter Interceptor MAX. SPEED: 589 km/h WEIGHT: 3,622 kg CREW: 1 ARMAMENT: .50 cal Browning M2 HMGs (6)
